{"claims":[{"claim_text":"If net neutrality were razed, Comcast might charge users $5 per month to visit popular free sites such as Facebook or Wikipedia, justifying the charge with labels such as “convenience fee” or “service fee”.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"If net neutrality were razed, Comcast’s action would stymie the flow of information to low-income Internet users, who are already subject to slow speeds and prohibitive broadband costs.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"If AT&T workers strike due to poor working conditions and create a website to publicize their grievances and seek support, AT&T might prevent its broadband subscribers from accessing it.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Preventing broadband subscribers from accessing a website created by striking AT&T workers would be an act of union-busting censorship.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
